Yes, you may re-submit your proposal which will then go through the independent evaluation process when being considered for funding. We recommend that any previous feedback is taken into consideration.

Can a non-UK based organisation receive funding?

A UK organisation must lead the consortium. A non-UK based organisation cannot receive national funding as the primary focus of the UK Space Agency is on the growth of the UK sector; therefore, any monies awarded cannot go outside the UK to a partner body. If the proposed non-UK capability is essential the work can be subcontracted out, however the proposal must demonstrate clearly that this resource is not available in the UK.

Does the organisational background information apply only to the lead organisation?

No. All proposals must include organisational background information for all those involved, therefore including those put forward in collaboration.

Who can submit an application?

Applications must be submitted by the lead organisation on behalf of a consortium. The lead applicant must demonstrate that it has the capability, capacity and governance arrangements required to act as the accountable body for a UK-wide, multi-year programme of this scale and complexity. All consortium partners must be identified in the application and provide the required confirmation of their commitment.

Applications must be submitted by 11:59 pm UK time, 20 January 2027 following the application guidance.

Does previous experience with the UK Space Agency confer any advantages or disadvantages on an applicant?

No, applications will be scored on their individual merit. However, successful delivery of past government funded projects would be a beneficial factor to detail in reference to the project team’s experience.

What is understood by staff cost?

Costs should be applied for any staff that will be part of the project team/work regardless of employment status within the organisation (i.e.: short/long-term fixed or permanent contracts). However, any costs for project work done by sub-contractors must be declared as a separate cost to the project. Sub-contractors cannot be partners to the project and justification in the proposal would need to be clearly stated as to the requirement for use of sub-contractors.

Please refer to the Call Guidance ‘Financial requirements’ and the UK Space Agency’s standard grant funding webpage for detail on “What costs will UK Space Agency grant funding cover?”

Do all project staff have to be identified/hired prior to submitting the project application?

No, not all staff have to be place/hired by submission of the proposal, but recruitment plans should indicate confidence that a position will be filled and the time required to do so must be contained within the project schedule.

Partnerships and consortia

Is there a way to link to others who are interested in joining a consortium? Would it be possible to share contact details with consent?

We will not be part of the matching process between consortium members. We have shared contact details of the attendees to our market engagement events and webinars who consented to their details being shared, including organisation, scale of activity and the ESERO-relevant activities and audiences they work with. This was designed to give attendees jumping-off points to explore consortium partnerships. However, it must be noted that our sharing of details does not represent an endorsement nor any other indication on behalf of the UK Space Agency bidders must undertake their own due diligence as to the suitability / capability of any consortia member or sub-contractor.

NEW: Can organisations bid in more than one consortium?

Organisations can bid into more than one consortium, provided each bid delivers against the outcomes and requirements of the funding call. However, the lead organisation must only submit one proposal as a lead, but can appear as a consortium partner or sub-contractor in another.

Will there be any guidance about consortium building, e.g. the level of detail in EU Horizon tender processes?

The UK Space Agency does not get involved in handling arrangements or agreements for consortia. Consortium agreement templates are widely available.

Are you trying to create a community vibe with the partners you work with, for example an ecosystem with quarterly meetings between consortium members?

The UK Space Agency supports a collaborative consortium approach, but the lead organisation is responsible for proposing appropriate governance, decision-making and engagement arrangements for consortium members. The application must identify all consortium members and include the required letters of intent. Formal Collaboration Agreements do not need to be completed at application stage, but must be signed within six weeks of completing the Grant Funding Agreement and must flow down the relevant grant terms and conditions.

Can the UK Space Agency provide advice about any type of collaboration / partnership programme that the Agency is promoting?

The Agency does not promote any particular collaboration although collaboration in essence is encouraged in projects.

Are there minimum or maximum numbers of partners that can be in a project consortium?

There are no minimum or maximum number of partners. However, we suggest each partner has a clear role within the project. If you require more than 7 partner organisations please contact ESERO-UKgrantcall@DSIT.gov.uk in good time before the proposal submission date so that we can provide support with the Flexigrant application form limitations.

Is there a difference between a partner and a sub-contractor?

Yes. If you are collaborating with another organisation or company, then they are your project partner and will be included in your proposal.

What are the audit requirements on the grant?

An independent reasonable assurance report is required as part of the total cost of the project. Confirmation will be required that the Grant Recipient has expended the sums in respect of the period in which the milestone payments have been claimed. For this purpose, a report must be completed within 6 months of the grant concluding. Reasonable assurance reports are an ineligible project cost (so can’t be claimed through the grant).

As part of the UK Space Agency Grant Funding Agreements, recipients should keep project documentation for seven years following the completion of the grant. The UK Space Agency commissions audits of grant projects through the Government Internal Assurance Agency (GIAA) each year and the grants may be subject to this scrutiny at any time.

Can I change the estimated costs?

You are able to edit the estimated costs by financial year and matched funding information, up to the point of submission. Once the proposal has been submitted you cannot change the costings.

NEW: Can organisations include pay increases as part of the financial proposal, if these are included at the outset?

Pay increases can be submitted as part of the applicant’s responses, the UK Space Agency will review these alongside all other eligible costs as part of our assessment.

NEW: What is the position on intellectual property for activities delivered through the grant?

Recipients would own the intellectual property (IP), and that the UK Space Agency would not retain ownership. The position under the ESA contract would differ: ESA would not acquire existing IP developed before the ESERO activity but would retain copyright or share rights in educational resources created during the programme, enabling resources and concepts to be reused across the wider ESERO network. These resources should be available to users free of charge.

NEW: Are the grant funds made in arrears?

The grant payment can be split in instalments, but UK Space Agency grant payments, in line with other government grant payments, must be made in arrears.

NEW: If an organisation already delivers an ESA programme, what additional work can ESERO-UK fund, and how should the responsibilities, costs and impacts be separated from existing commitments?

Organisations can hold other ESA contracts, but each contract has its own deliverables and activities should not overlap. Collaboration and synergies between programmes are possible, but ESERO-UK should not be used simply to co-fund or strengthen outreach activity that is already funded under another ESA programme.

NEW: As this is a three-year programme, staff specifically recruited for the programme could acquire redundancy rights. Can redundancy payments be claimed?

ESA uses a firm fixed price arrangement. Providers are responsible for accounting for relevant employment costs within their agreed price. Annual changes in hourly rates can be anticipated in the financial forms, but the final activity must remain within the agreed budget. UK Space Agency will not include redundancy payments as an eligible cost as part of the Grant Funding Agreement so these will not be claimable once the grant-funded period ends. With regards annual pay increases, like ESA, these can be accounted for in your proposal for UK Space Agency’s review.

Applying through Flexigrant

How do I register for Flexigrant to apply for the ESERO-UK Call?

Flexigrant is an online grant management tool being used to manage the ESERO-UK Call. To apply, you will need to register for Flexigrant via the Portal homepage - DSIT Grants. Once you have signed in you should be able to see on the Application Portal the details for applying to the ESERO-UK Call.

Can I request multiple users to view the same application?

You can enable the ‘application collaboration’ setting which allows the lead applicant to invite others (as long as you have a Flexigrant account) to view/complete the application with them. For instructions on this, select the Participants tab on the Summary page and add participants. This will then send an invite to collaborate on the application to the email address provided. The lead applicant is responsible for checking and submitting the final application. Collaborators or co-applicants can be deleted at any time during the application process.

Do I need to add all collaborators and partners to the application?

Yes. All consortium partners intended to deliver the project must be listed in the Organisation Details section of the Flexigrant application. A letter of intent from each consortium partner must be uploaded with the application to confirm its commitment and authorisation for the lead organisation to act on its behalf.

Can I work on the application over a period of time?

Yes, as long as you submit before the proposal deadline on 23:59(GMT) 20 January 2027, you are welcome to edit your application and save progress as you go. The portal allows you to edit each part of the application at any time as follows:

i. Main Details

ii. Organisation Details

iii. Estimated Costs

iv. Proposal

v. Letters of Support

vi. Declaration

The portal times out after two hours. Please ensure you save progress as you go or have backed up answers elsewhere, so as not to lose any changes.
